minutes.headline: Sewer Commission voted to require a bond for the full project on the private 42 Highland Street sewer extension.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a resident ask to add 236 Crossroad to the Whum/Pratt Street sewer extension, then got a design update from Wright-Pierce covering rock found in borings, a switch to low-pressure sewer on Pratt Street, and the SRF loan application. It changed its earlier vote so the 42 Highland Street private extension needs a bond for the full project value. It also covered the Whum luxury apartments sewer fee dispute, inflow/infiltration enforcement, capital plan items, the FY15 budget and invoices.

public_comment.topic: Asked the commission to include 236 Crossroad in the sewer extension and offered an easement.
Said she wants sewer for her lot because of an old septic system and had not known about the project.

votes.motion: Approve the bond for the full amount of the 42 Highland private sewer extension project, naming the town as obligee.

budget_items.topic: SRF loan for the sewer extension
budget_items.what_was_said: The project is funded through a state revolving fund loan at a low rate; the application is due October 15th.
First invoice covered initial coordination, wetlands, surveys and early drawings.
Second invoice covered field survey, geotech work and SRF application preparation, and includes the survey subcontractor amount.
The contractor's agent said an insurance bond is costly and proposed cash instead.
Privilege and connection fees were described; the developer says it can only afford a much smaller sewer cost.
The commission has money budgeted for the next infiltration project and wants an updated engineering proposal.
Budget looked encouraging; user charge revenue is based on commitments and runs below the year's share because billing is quarterly.
Two invoices for legal work were presented, with a concern that extension-related costs be tracked separately.
The bill was higher than members remembered and they asked to review the proposal.

decisions.decision: Wright-Pierce to review the CWMP for parcel 236 Crossroad and report back on whether it can be served.
Confirm with town counsel whether a cash tri-party account can replace a bond; contractor to supply a schedule of values and engineer letter by October 14th.
Commission holds its position on the Whum apartments fees; Dan Hill to recheck the fee effective dates.
Capital plan input to be finalized at the October 14th meeting, with Small Water asked for pump station and SCADA recommendations in writing.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to require a bond for the full project value on the private 42 Highland Street sewer extension, naming the town as obligee.
The commission asked Wright-Pierce to review the town's wastewater plan for 236 Crossroad and report whether the lot can be served by the extension.
Wright-Pierce gave a design update on the Whum/Pratt Street extension, and the project is funded by a state revolving fund loan with the application due October 15th.
The commission will confirm with town counsel whether a cash tri-party account can replace a bond, with contractor documents due October 14th.
The commission held its position on the Whum apartments sewer fees, and Dan Hill will recheck the fee effective dates.

why_it_matters: The bond requirement decides who carries the cost if a privately built sewer extension is left unfinished, which bears on whether the risk falls on the developer or on sewer users and taxpayers.
Whether 236 Crossroad and other lots can join the extension, and what the Whum apartments pay in sewer fees, affect who connects to town sewer and how the cost is shared among ratepayers.
watch_next: October 14th: the commission is to finalize capital plan input, and the contractor is to supply a schedule of values and an engineer letter.
October 15th: the state revolving fund loan application for the sewer extension is due.
